newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-MCMILLAN PUTS SOUTH AFRICA IN HEALTHY POSITION.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-MCMILLAN PUTS SOUTH AFRICA IN HEALTHY POSITION.

text.p: A half-century from Brian McMillan helped South Africa into a healthy position against Australia at tea on the second day of the third and final cricket test match at Centurion Park on Saturday.
The burly all-rounder had been promoted to number three in the batting line-up to shore up South Africa's fragile top order and he immediately obliged.

He was finally caught for 55 off bat and pad at short leg in the first over of off-spin from Mark Waugh but not before posting a vital century partnership with Adam Bacher (51 not out) -- South Africa's first of the series.
At tea South Africa were 145 for two in reply to Australia's 227.
The value of McMillan's innings was highlighted by the fact that it was the first half-century from a South African number three in the first innings in the 20-test reign of coach Bob Woolmer.

He and Bacher both suffered a torrid time against the leg spin of Shane Warne -- who repeatedly beat the outside edge -- while McMillan was twice struck on the helmet as he attempted to hook Jason Gillespie.
He survived to post his second half century of the series in just over two hours, striking seven fours from 100 balls.
Bacher, who had taken 50 minutes to get off the mark, showed commendable patience, contributing just 34 of century stand, before reaching his own half-century in just under four hours.
Earlier opener Gary Kirsten had become Ian Healy's 300th test victim when he got a thin edge to Glenn McGrath to give the keeper a straightforward catch.
Australia have already won the series after victories in Johannesburg and Port Elizabeth.
